newsitem.title: USA: State legislatures cut $4 bln in taxes - report.
newsitem.headline: State legislatures cut $4 bln in taxes - report.

text.p: State legislatures approved a net tax reduction of $4 billion in the current fiscal year, according to a report this week by the National Conference of State Legislatures.
The reduction followed $3.3 billion of tax cuts during fiscal 1996, marking the first time legislatures have cut taxes for two consecutive years since 1978 and 1979, the report said.
Leading the tax cut charge was New York State, which completed a multi-year income tax reduction adopted in 1995 with by cutting $2 billion.
Connecticut followed with a $268 million reduction in personal income, coporate income and hospital taxes that was also part of a multi-year tax cut package started in 1995, according to the report.
Other states where taxes were cut include California, Indiana, North Carolina, Ohio, Massachusetts and New Jersey.
While tax cuts totalling more than $4 billion had been expected by some due to the healthy fiscal condition of most states, the report said that two factors may have prevented larger reductions.

"First, states remain wary of federal spending reductions and the impact on their budgets, and many are keeping large reserves for such a contingency; and second, a dozen or more states have already cut taxes in the last few years," the report stated.
Missouri and Idaho were the only two states that raised taxes significantly, the report said.
Missouri raised its gasoline tax by two cents per gallon and Idaho by four cents per gallon.
